title: Pair Programming Misconceptions
summary: Martin Fowler (2006) corrects misconceptions: agile does not mandate pairing, pairing does not halve productivity because typing is not the hard part, and rote code is a smell.

assertions.quote: The manifesto doesn't mention pair programming and most agile methods don't make it part of their approach.

verdicts.note: The Agile Manifesto lists values and principles, not practices.

The review's table of agile methods lists pair programming among XP's twelve practices, while the descriptions of Scrum, Crystal, DSDM, FDD and Lean and the agile manifesto's four values make no mention of it.

assertions.quote: a pair is actually more productive that two separate developers. This is due to the continuous discussion and review
that would be true if the hardest part of programming was typing
They gave it a try, expecting to hate it, and found they really liked it.
writing boring rote code is a smell. If I'm writing boring repetitive code it's usually a sign that I've missed an important abstraction
